chinhDien: Sect Grand Hall (Tông Môn Đại Điện 宗門大殿): the main hall of an immortal cultivation sect. Two-tier hip-and-gable roof with dark grey tiles and strongly upturned eave tips, a small gold finial on top. Six cinnabar-red pillars across the front veranda, wooden lattice doors behind them, a raised carved stone platform with a short flight of steps at the front. Dignified, ancient, slightly mystical.
tinhXa: Disciple Quarters (Đệ Tử Tĩnh Xá 弟子靜舍): a modest one-storey wooden dwelling for outer-sect disciples. Single curved tile roof with upturned corners, four red pillars, paper lattice windows, a low stone base. Simple, quiet, lived-in: a broom by the door, a small potted pine.
tuLinhTran: Qi Gathering Array (Tụ Linh Trận 聚靈陣): a FLAT, LOW round stone disc lying on the ground like a millstone — its thickness is only about one tenth of its diameter, NOT a tall drum or pedestal. On its top surface: a carved ring of Chinese seal-script talisman characters and a faint jade-green circle. In the center a slim jade obelisk, topped with a small floating gold crystal. Wisps of pale ink mist rise from the runes. No walls, no roof.
duocVien: Herb Garden (Dược Viên 藥園): four neat raised beds of medicinal spirit herbs in dark soil, small leafy plants in jade green, bordered by low bamboo edging. No building, only the garden plot on its footprint.
